en.title: Dune 3 Trailer Reveals Most Important Character: It's Not Paul
en.summary: The first glimpse of Dune: Part Three is here, and it’s already shaking up the franchise's central narrative. A shocking revelation from the latest trailer positions a familiar face as the saga's true linchpin.
en.body:
The sands of Arrakis are about to shift once more, and the first trailer for **Dune: Part Three** has just dropped a bombshell: the most crucial character in the entire **Dune** saga isn't **Paul Atreides** at all. While **Timothée Chalamet**'s prescient messiah grapples with the galactic jihad he unleashed, the real narrative engine appears to be a figure we thought we knew.

The trailer plunges us back into the fractured lives of **Paul** and **Chani** (**Zendaya**), showcasing her disillusionment with his ascent to power. Meanwhile, **Princess Irulan** (**Florence Pugh**), daughter of the deposed Emperor **Shaddam IV** (**Christopher Walken**), is drawn into a shadowy conspiracy orchestrated by the shape-shifting **Face Dancer Scytale** (**Robert Pattinson**). But the most significant reveal is the presence of a character known as **Hayt**. For fans of the books, this name is synonymous with a resurrected, deeply changed **Duncan Idaho** (**Jason Momoa**). Once the loyal swordmaster, **Duncan Idaho**’s sacrifice in the first film allowed **Paul** and **Lady Jessica** (**Rebecca Ferguson**) to escape the Harkonnen onslaught, setting the stage for his eventual return in a form that will challenge **Paul**'s very destiny.

## The Return of a Legend, Reimagined

**Duncan Idaho** has always been a fan favorite, a beacon of loyalty and martial prowess. **Jason Momoa**’s charismatic portrayal in the first film cemented this, showcasing **Duncan**’s vital role in forging alliances with the Fremen, particularly **Stilgar** (**Javier Bardem**). His death was a pivotal moment, a heroic act that underscored the brutal stakes of the Harkonnen invasion. However, **Frank Herbert**’s novels delve far deeper into **Duncan**’s fate, introducing the concept of genetic memory and resurrection. The trailer’s focus on **Hayt** suggests that **Dune: Part Three** will explore this complex arc, positioning him not merely as a resurrected warrior but as a potentially pivotal force in the ongoing conflict and **Paul**'s internal struggles.

## Why Hayt Matters More Than You Think

This shift in focus from **Paul** to **Hayt** (the resurrected **Duncan Idaho**) is a profound testament to the intricate tapestry of **Frank Herbert**’s universe. **Hayt** represents more than just a skilled fighter; he embodies the consequences of **Paul**'s actions and the cyclical nature of violence and prophecy. The **Face Dancer Scytale**'s involvement, and **Hayt**'s central role in his machinations, hints at a narrative that will explore themes of identity, manipulation, and the true cost of power. For the **Dune** faithful, this is the kind of deep-dive adaptation they’ve been waiting for, promising to unpack the philosophical and political complexities that make the books so enduring.

## What's Next

While an official release date for **Dune: Part Three** has not yet been announced, the trailer’s debut signals that production is well underway. Fans can anticipate further details and a more comprehensive look at **Hayt** and the unfolding galactic conflict in the coming months.

content_raw: This article contains spoilers for Dune: Part Three and several Frank Herbert books. It’s not really about Paul Atreides. Paul may be Lisan al-Gaib, he may be the Kwisatz Haderach, but Paul is not actually the main character of the Dune franchise. Instead, that honor goes to the character introduced in the latest trailer for Dune: Part Three , the character you knew as Duncan Idaho. The latest trailer shows the internal fractures in Paul’s ( Timothée Chalamet ) life as he continues the Fremen jihad launched after he dethroned Padishah Emperor Shaddam IV ( Christopher Walken ) at the end of the previous movie. His partner Chani ( Zendaya ) feels betrayed by his actions and his legal wife, Shaddam IV’s daughter Princess Irulan ( Florence Pugh ) joins the plot that the Face Dancer Scytale ( Robert Pattinson ) launches against him. Central to this conspiracy is the introduction of the man we first met as Duncan Idaho, played by Jason Momoa . Despite what he appears to be, this man is actually called Hayt, and he is the most important character in Frank Herbert ‘s Dune novels. With his incongruous name and skill in battle, Duncan Idaho was one of the standout characters of the first Dune movie. Played by a chummy Momoa, Duncan went ahead to scout Arrakis for Duke Leto ( Oscar Isaac ), where he befriended Stilgar ( Javier Bardem ) of the Freman and formed alliances that would allow Paul to defeat the usurper Baron Harkonnen ( Stellan Skarsgård ). However, when Harkonnen’s forces first attacked and killed Leto, Duncan sacrificed himself to allow Paul and his mother Jessica ( Rebecca Ferguson ) to escape, setting into motion his final ascension as Lisan al-Gaib. Although the world of Dune is full of dissemblances and secrets, Duncan’s death was not faked. He did indeed die battling Harkonnen’s elite Sardaukar. But as viewers of the HBO series Dune: Prophecy already know, cloning exists in the franchise. An invention of the Bene Tleilax (a sect like the Bene Gesserit, except they work through technology instead of religion), clones or “gholas” are a mistrusted, but real part of the world. Yet, if someone was lonely enough, if someone missed the person who had been cloned and wants to recreate those experiences, then they may accept the gholas, despite their misgivings. Which is exactly what Scytale plans. Directed by Denis Villeneuve, who co-wrote the screenplay with comic book scribe Brian K. Vaughan, and based on the 1969 novel Dune Messiah , Dune: Part Three sees Paul start to crack under the pressure of enacting his master plan. While his prescience convinces him that brutal measures are needed to save humanity, others doubt him, which makes Paul feel lonely. Enter Scytale, who preys on that loneliness by bringing back the man who once loved and protected Paul, who provided the direction and security who so desperately wants. But Hayt is not Duncan.
